evidence: app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:48 — `@Service()` decorator, the newest API in the codebase (added and marked stable in Angular v22, June 2026), on the app's central data-loading service
app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:32 — `linkedSignal` (stable since v20, May 2025) for search text that follows the URL except while typing
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/move-table.ts:84 — `linkedSignal` (stable since v20) for per-table sort state
app/src/app/app.config.server.ts:11-13 — `provideServerRendering(withRoutes(...))` (stable since v20.2) and `provideAppInitializer` (stable since v19)
app/src/app/main.server.ts:5 — `BootstrapContext` third arg to `bootstrapApplication` (stable since v20.3)
reach.rationale: No experimental/preview APIs at all; the only sub-6-months-stable API is `@Service()` (v22, ~5 months old), sitting in a central place (page data loading), with the rest being long-stable modern APIs used centrally.

evidence: app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:48 — `@Service()` appears on exactly one class; swapping back to `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` is a one-line change
app/src/app/app.config.server.ts:11-13 — server-only newer APIs (provideServerRendering, withRoutes, provideAppInitializer) confined to the server config merged via mergeApplicationConfig
app/src/app/pages/not-found/not-found.ts:14 — RESPONSE_INIT used once, optionally injected, with a null guard for browser/SSG
app/src/app/app.ts:45 — afterNextRender used once with an explicit injector
app/angular.json:1-80 — no experimental builder flags or configuration toggles anywhere
containment.rationale: The single very-new API is a one-line decorator on one service, and all other modern API usage is isolated to config files or single components; nothing risky is spread across many files.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:32-34 — linkedSignal is the textbook tool for 'writable state that follows a source but defers during pending user input'; an effect-based workaround would be more code
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/move-table.ts:84-86 — linkedSignal resets the sort when the table (game) changes — precisely its documented purpose, no stable alternative is simpler
app/src/app/pages/not-found/not-found.ts:14-16 — RESPONSE_INIT is the only supported way to emit a real 404 status in SSR; a spec/SEO requirement
app/src/app/data/page-data.ts:48-65 — @Service() matches current v22 framework guidance (angular.dev tutorials now teach it) and the class uses inject() only, fitting its constraints
app/src/app/app.config.ts:21 — withEventReplay() guards user events during hydration of a data-heavy SSR page; stable since v19
justification.rationale: Every non-trivial use buys something a stable alternative couldn't do as simply (linkedSignal's source-linked reset, RESPONSE_INIT for 404 status), and the one brand-new API (@Service) is ergonomics-only but one line to swap and aligns with current official guidance; nothing is novelty for its own sake.

findings.issue: `@Service()` is the newest API in the app (introduced and stabilized in Angular v22, June 2026); being a current-major API it may still see minor iteration, unlike the long-stable `@Injectable`.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is since it matches current official guidance; if the team prefers maximum maturity, use `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` — a one-line, behavior-equivalent change.

findings.issue: The linkedSignal computation relies on tracking `pushedQ` side state to distinguish URL-driven changes from the user's own debounced typing, which is subtle; linkedSignal itself is stable since v20 and not a risk.
findings.suggestion: Consider simplifying the debounce to a plain signal + timer without linkedSignal, or add a comment noting the invariant; no API-risk action needed.

summary: The app rides the current stable release (Angular v22.2) with zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs and no experimental build flags; its measured `experimental` markers are empty and code inspection confirms it. The only recently-stable API is the new `@Service()` decorator (v22, ~5 months old), used once on a single, trivially-swappable service. All other modern usage (linkedSignal, RESPONSE_INIT, provideServerRendering/withRoutes, BootstrapContext, withEventReplay) is long-stable and each use is well-justified and contained.
